title: SOBAT-PS
tagline: A government information system still live on kaltaraprov.go.id, three years after delivery.
summary: The social forestry and community empowerment information system of the Forestry Office of North Kalimantan Province: forest-farmer groups, their business units, assistance programs, grant recipients, and aid proposals in one place.
role: Contract web developer: built the system, reviewed code, debugged, and wrote training documentation.

case_study.problem: The Forestry Office needed one place to track social forestry groups, their business units, assistance programs, grant recipients, and the aid proposals members submit.
case_study.role: Delivered the system under contract (April 2022 to September 2023), then carried it through an internship version and a thesis API, and rebuilt it on Laravel 10.
decisions: Laravel with server-rendered Bootstrap views and DataTables for the list and detail screens office staff use.
A separate Lumen 10 API with JWT authentication for the thesis, kept apart from the web app.
A Laravel 10 rebuild of the website with improvements.
case_study.outcome: The system is still live on the provincial government domain (checked 24 October 2026).

title: PolicySemVer
tagline: A versioning GitHub Action and npm CLI, v1.0.1, listed on GitHub Marketplace.
summary: Policy-first semantic versioning for deployed apps: the major version comes from an environment variable, a pull request gets a dry-run comment with the next version, and the version, tag, and release are written only after merge.
role: Sole author: design, implementation, tests, docs, and releases.

case_study.problem: Release tools built for library monorepos fit deployed apps poorly: apps need a manual major version, commits like 'feat & fix:', and a way to sync prod back to dev without a version bump.
case_study.role: Designed and built the core library, the CLI, and the GitHub Action, then published all three.
decisions: Three artifacts from one pnpm monorepo: @policy-semver/core, the policy-semver CLI, and the Action.
The Action runs committed dist/index.js, so consumers install no runtime dependencies.
Major bumps stay manual through APP_VERSION_MAJOR; pull requests only get a sticky dry-run comment, and writes happen after merge.
Unknown config keys are rejected, and the commit classifier is covered by ranked fixtures (Vitest).
case_study.outcome: v1.0.1 released on 2 September 2026, listed on GitHub Marketplace and published to npm.

metrics.label: Latest release
metrics.source: npm view policy-semver version; GitHub releases

title: Wedding Invitation
tagline: An invitation with RSVP and guest check-in, turned into a static archive after the event.
summary: A digital wedding invitation with personalized guest links, RSVP, a guestbook, and an admin panel for check-in. After the wedding it became a read-only static archive and the backend was retired.
role: Sole developer of the invitation and its admin backend.

case_study.problem: An invitation that guests open once, on their phones, must load fast, handle retries without duplicate RSVPs, and protect guest and gift details.
case_study.role: Built the Next.js invitation, the Laravel + Filament admin with a check-in flow, and the switch to a static archive.
decisions: RSVP and guestbook writes carry an Idempotency-Key header; in-flight conflicts return 409 instead of creating duplicates.
A strict Content Security Policy with per-directive allowlists, and the Supabase service key kept server-only.
Below-the-fold sections load with next/dynamic; only the hero, the invitation, and the music player are static imports.
After the event, production data was frozen into a server-only snapshot, the page was prerendered, and the backend was retired, so guest names and account numbers no longer reach the browser.
case_study.outcome: The invitation now runs as a static archive with a single remaining function; no guest data is published.

title: NIKKE Progression Calculator
tagline: Three services, one database: a Next.js app, a NestJS API, and a Laravel admin panel.
summary: A progression calculator for the game NIKKE. Players plan resources and skill costs; an admin panel maintains the master data the calculator uses.
role: Sole developer of all three services.

case_study.problem: A calculator, its API, and an admin panel for master data each fit a different framework and host, but they must agree on one set of data.
case_study.role: Designed the split into three services and built each one.
decisions: The NestJS API owns the schema through Prisma migrations; the Laravel admin only reads and writes rows and never migrates Prisma-owned tables.
A guard blocks destructive Artisan commands (migrate:fresh, db:wipe) when they target the production database.
Each service deploys natively to its host (Vercel, Railway, Laravel Cloud), with path-filtered CI per package.
The admin panel connects through the Supabase pooler instead of a managed database, so all three services share one Postgres.
case_study.outcome: Three independently deployable services sharing one Supabase Postgres database.

title: Timetables
tagline: Multi-stage festival schedules with clash detection, in the visitor's own time zone.
summary: Festival schedules across several stages: a timeline per stage, a personal agenda of favorite slots with clash detection, times shown in the device's time zone, and bulk import for organizers.

case_study.problem: Festival-goers juggle overlapping sets on several stages, often across time zones, and organizers need to enter hundreds of slots quickly.
case_study.role: Built v1 in SvelteKit, then started a v2 rewrite in Next.js 16 on Cloudflare.
decisions: v1 (SvelteKit on Cloudflare Pages + D1): timeline and agenda views, favorites, clash detection, shareable URL state, PWA, and a manage area with text and CSV bulk import that previews valid and failed rows before saving.
v2 moves to Next.js 16 + OpenNext on Cloudflare Workers with Drizzle + D1, built on the open-source Studio Admin template for the dashboard shell.
Time-zone handling lives in small tested utilities, with check scripts for parsing, streams, and time zones.
case_study.outcome: v1 was feature-complete in July 2026; v2 is in progress. Its manage-area pattern is the basis for this portfolio's manage area.

title: This portfolio
tagline: An admin panel you can inspect, with an architecture diagram for every private system.
summary: This site: a public admin panel without login, a read-only public API, and a protected manage area for content, running on Cloudflare Workers.

case_study.problem: A tech lead cannot read a candidate's private code, so the portfolio itself has to be a system worth inspecting.
case_study.role: Planned, designed, built, and deployed the site.
decisions: Next.js 16 + Hono + Drizzle on Cloudflare Workers through OpenNext, with D1 for content and R2 for files.

While building it, every page hung after the first content update. The cause was a cache bug between Next.js 16.4 and Workers (opennextjs-cloudflare#1464, vercel/next.js#100345); the cache was removed and pages read straight from D1 on every request.
The manage area sits behind a secret runtime path, Cloudflare Access, and a server-side check on every action, so the repository can stay public.
case_study.outcome: Live on Cloudflare Workers. Performance numbers are added from real measurements before launch.

title: PT HTSI web profile
tagline: Company website and service quotation requests on WordPress.
summary: The company website of PT Heat Transfer Solutions Indonesia, built with WordPress and Brizy (2022-2023), including a system for receiving service quotation requests.
